messages.subject: Re: Creating a shortcut to run a <rook app> ?!
parts:
Hi Tal,

To serve a page, one just needs to start R, start Rook, load the app then point a browser to right url.

From within an R session one just has to call `load_app("scriptname.R")`. This will call browseURL to open the script. Alternatively, one can pass in the argument `open_page=FALSE` and then point your browser to http://localhost:PORT/custom/scriptname

There is a file Rook.sh (https://github.com/jverzani/gWidgetsWWW2/blob/master/inst/nginx/Rook.sh) to start R and Rook to run a script from the command line, not from within an R session. This script is modified from Start.sh that Jeff wrote https://gist.github.com/6d09536d871c1a648a84

To create a desktop shortcut would require executing the commands in Rook.sh from shortcut.

Hope that helps. --John

messages.subject: Re: R: Creating a shortcut to run a <rook app> ?!
parts: Hi Tal and all,

> I just came across this post:
> http://www.r-bloggers.com/r-creating-a-shortcut-to-run-a-gwidgets-gui/
> Suggesting how to Creating a shortcut to run a gWidgets GUI, and
> wondered if any of you found a solution for doing this with a rook
> application.
> I suspect the solution proposed in the post might be also used for
> rook.
> Any thoughts?

Not about the post (which I did not read), but here is how I do it.
Hope it helps.

Sven

PS: I have no idea whether my approach is elegant or rubbish. If
anyone can evaluate, please let me know!


== (1) Windows batch (.bat) file (to which the shortcut points): ==

@echo off
COLOR E0
echo.
echo To finish please click 'logout' in your browser.
echo.
"C:\Programme\R\R-2.14.1\bin\i386\Rterm.exe" --no-restore --no-save <
"\\path\to\script\startup.R" > "\\path\to\logfile.txt" 2>&1
echo.
echo Done.
echo.
pause


== (2) The startup.R file: ==

#!/usr/bin/Rscript --vanilla

## I use the same script as an executable in GNU/Linux, otherwise you
## probably would not need the above line.

setwd("\\\\path\\to\\script\\")

library(RMySQL, quietly=TRUE)
library(Rook, quietly=TRUE)
source("config.R")
source("functions.R")

dbcon <- startMysql()
app <- Builder$new(Static$new(urls=c("/css", "/js"), root="."),
Brewery$new(url="/brew", root="."),
Redirect$new("/brew/index.rhtml"))
s <- Rhttpd$new()
s$add(app=app, name="mycoolapp")
s$start(quiet=TRUE)
s$browse("mycoolapp")

## After logout is clicked in the browser, SESS("r-logout") will
## return TRUE.
while(!isTRUE(SESS("r-logout"))) {
Sys.sleep(5)
}

dbDisconnect(dbcon)

cat("Bye!\n")

messages.author: 3d0cccc7ec805901
messages.subject: Re: R: Creating a shortcut to run a <rook app> ?!
parts: Hi Tal and all,

> > Is there a chance you might send a simple ZIP file with an example
> > project one could run?

Yes, I attach it to this email, WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY.

You need to rename startRookApp.bat.txt to startRookApp.bat (without
the .txt extension). (This is because Google does not distribute this
email otherwise.)

In startRookApp.bat you have to adjust the path to R.
In startup.R you have to adjust the path for setwd().

Again: I have no idea whether my approach is elegant or not. It is
more of a "quick and dirty" solution rather than a bullet proof app.

Sven
